"No single organization, funding source, or individual could have built what we see here today," said commissioner Ida Rukavina at the ribbon cutting. stories.extended_summary: More than 750 people in North Carolina who were homeless now have keys to their own place — and zero federal dollars were involved. The Lotus Campaign, a Charlotte nonprofit, covers the small stuff that blocks housing: renter's insurance, application fees, security deposits. Then it connects each person with local wraparound services and gives landlords a direct line when issues come up. The results are striking: 90% of participants stayed housed after their first year, and fewer than 5% returned to homelessness. Founder Beth Silverman, who came from real estate development, built the model after watching the public, private, and nonprofit sectors each drop the ball. "This is not easy by any means," she says.
